sections.h2: Where is Santa Fe and why is it different from other New Mexico cities?
sections.html:
Santa Fe is the capital of New Mexico and the county seat of Santa Fe County. It lies at the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains at 6,998 feet, the highest elevation of any U.S. state capital.

The city covers about 52.4 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 87,505 residents. Founded in 1610 as the capital of Nuevo México, it is the oldest state capital in the United States. It became capital of the U.S. Territory of New Mexico in 1851 and the state capital in 1912.

That age shows up in the housing. Santa Fe is known for adobe-style Pueblo Revival and Territorial Revival architecture, much of it preserved and protected, so a seller here may own a house shaped by rules that do not apply in other cities.

sections.h2: What does the Santa Fe economy look like?
sections.html:
Government is the largest employer in Santa Fe, with roughly 15,000 jobs, followed by education and health services and by leisure and hospitality.

SectorApproximate jobs
Government15,000
Education and health services11,600
Leisure and hospitality10,900

Tourism and the arts are central. The city has more than 250 art galleries and hosts the Santa Fe International Folk Art Market, the Traditional Spanish Colonial Market and Indian Market. About one-tenth of all employment is tied to artistic and cultural industries. Los Alamos National Laboratory is about a 45-minute drive away.

Because so many jobs depend on the state government and visitors, local demand can shift with budgets and travel seasons, and a seller should ask any buyer how long they need to close.

sections.h2: What is the wider Santa Fe region?
sections.html:
The Santa Fe metropolitan area has an estimated 158,000 people, and the greater Albuquerque, Santa Fe and Los Alamos combined statistical area spans eight counties and 1.16 million residents.

Santa Fe Plaza, the Palace of the Governors and the Santa Fe Historic District anchor the center, and the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum and Meow Wolf are among its cultural draws. In 2005 Santa Fe became the first U.S. city inducted into the UNESCO Creative Cities Network.

The Rail Runner Express serves the city through four stations: Santa Fe Depot, South Capitol, Zia Road and Santa Fe County/NM 599.

sections.h2: How does Santa Fe's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Santa Fe averages 12.79 inches of precipitation and 20.2 inches of snow a year. The 24-hour average temperature runs from 30.3°F in December to 70.1°F in July, so heating is a real cost for much of the year.

Wildfire is also a local concern. The Santa Fe Fire Department says it is one of the only fire departments in New Mexico with ten full-time employees who specialize in fuel management in the Wildland Urban Interface. It offers free Wildfire Home Hazard Assessments and evacuation zone information. If your house backs onto open land, an assessment report can show a buyer what you have done.

  • Ask the fire department for a home hazard assessment before listing.
  • Keep records of any brush clearing or roof work.
  • Check your homeowner insurance terms, since buyers ask about them.

sections.h2: What historic district rules apply when selling in Santa Fe?
sections.html:
Santa Fe has five historic districts, and the Historic Districts Review Board (HDRB) reviews alterations that cannot be approved by staff. The board is a quasi-judicial body that designates historic status of structures, approves new construction and reviews changes to existing ones. The city lists its meetings for the second and fourth Tuesday of the month.

The city's Historic Preservation Division says it preserves the character of Santa Fe by administering the Historic Districts and Archaeological Districts ordinances. A buyer who wants to change a front facade, windows or walls in a district may need review first.

If your house sits in one of the districts, tell any buyer early, and ask the Historic Preservation Division what is on file for the address. The division lists historicpreservation@santafenm.gov for questions and hpdsubmittal@santafenm.gov for submittals, so you can ask what has been approved or filed for your address in writing.

sections.h2: What other Santa Fe rules affect a home sale?
sections.html:
The most common city rule for sellers is the short-term rental permit. Santa Fe requires every short-term rental to hold a business registration and either a Residential Short-Term Rental Permit or a Non-Residential Short-Term Rental Registration, depending on zoning. Anyone planning to own or run a short-term rental in calendar year 2026 must obtain a permit, and within 10 days of issuance or renewal the owner must notify required parties by first-class mail.

If your house has run as a rental, hand the buyer the permit status in writing. A new owner cannot assume the permit is theirs without checking the city's rules.

Schools are covered by Santa Fe Public Schools. Interstate 25, U.S. 84, U.S. 285 and NM 599 serve the city, and the Rail Runner Express stops at four Santa Fe stations. Santa Fe Regional Airport handles local flights.

sections.h2: How do Santa Fe County property taxes work?
sections.html:
The Santa Fe County Assessor values property and the Santa Fe County Treasurer collects the tax. The treasurer sends about 60,000 real property, personal property and mobile home tax bills each year.

ItemDetail
Notice of Value, 2026Mailed May 1, 2026, with 30 days from mailing to appeal or apply for exemptions
Bills mailedOn or before November 1
First halfDue November 10, delinquent after December 10
Second halfDue on or before May 10
Interest1% a month after 30 days, per the treasurer
Penalty1% a month, capped at 5%, with a $5 minimum
Assessor phone505-986-6300
Treasurer office100 Catron St, Santa Fe

In 2026 the county said a change from House Bill 285 widens the disabled veterans' exemption, so veterans with a service-connected disability rating below 100% are now eligible for a portion of it. If you are selling a house that carried this exemption, ask the assessor how the exemption transfers.

The treasurer's site lists a card fee of 2.5% and a flat $1.95 e-check fee on its payment platforms, so ask how a payment at closing will be made before you assume a method.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house fast in Santa Fe?
sections.html:
A Santa Fe seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer.

  • List with an agent: gives wide exposure but may involve inspections, repair requests and staging for a Santa Fe buyer.
  • Sell on your own: saves a commission but leaves paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • Cash offer: from a buyer who buys the house as it stands. Ask for the offer in writing and read it closely.

Cash sales often fit owners who inherited a house, hold a vacant second home, or face repairs on an older adobe. Whichever route you pick, gather the tax bill, any HDRB paperwork, rental permits and repair records before you talk to a buyer.

faqs.q: What county is Santa Fe in?
faqs.a: Santa Fe is in Santa Fe County, and it is the county seat as well as the state capital.

faqs.q: When are Santa Fe County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed on or before November 1. The first half is due November 10 and becomes delinquent after December 10, and the second half is due on or before May 10.

faqs.q: How many historic districts does Santa Fe have?
faqs.a: The city's Historic Preservation page says there are five historic districts. The Historic Districts Review Board reviews work that staff cannot approve administratively.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Santa Fe?
faqs.a: Yes. Every short-term rental needs a business registration and a permit or registration, depending on zoning, and an owner who plans to operate in 2026 must obtain an STR permit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Santa Fe house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer buys as-is, and a listed sale can also close without repairs if the buyer agrees. Compare what you would net on each route.
